notes: Nurturing relates to care; poisonous relates to harm/general badness.
Disarming suggests reducing threat/harm (care); creepy is generally negative.
Inspiring relates to striving for elevated/noble (purity); both have general moral valence.
Relates to spirituality and elevated/carnal aspects (purity); general moral valence.
Maturity relates to self-discipline/self-improvement (purity); general moral valence.
Idealism can relate to striving for an elevated way (purity) and general moral good.
Nihilism rejects elevated meaning (purity) and moral frameworks (general); Existentialism emphasizes individual freedom (liberty).
Directly relates to spirituality and sacredness (purity).
Classical relates to tradition (authority); avant-garde relates to challenging norms (liberty).
Complimentary relates to kindness (care); insulting relates to emotional harm (care) and general vice.
Communal relates to ingroup (loyalty); individualist can relate to ingroup vice (loyalty) and individual freedom (liberty).
Equitable relates to fairness; hypocritical relates to unfairness and general vice.
Traditional relates to respect for traditions (authority); unorthodox relates to defiance of norms (authority vice) and freedom (liberty).
Relates to self-discipline/self-improvement (purity); general moral valence.
